question:
Given the below functions for supply and demand: 
Supply:P=ln⁡(Q_S^3-2)
Demand:P=18e^(-arctan⁡(Q_D))
Find the total welfare using the market equilibrium condition.

1.text:
For the static competitive equilibrium the price that the buyers are willing to pay
has to be the price that is needed to cover marginal cost

$$
P_{S}(Q)=P_{D}(Q)\iff
\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q}\equiv P^{*}(Q)
\tag{1}
$$

and $Q_{S}=Q_{D}=Q^{*}$ on the equilibrium.  (1) is transcendental.
Put

$$
f(Q)=\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)-18\,e^{-\arctan Q}\; ,
\qquad Q>\sqrt[3]{2}\; .
$$

$f(4.6)<0<f(4.7)$ and a Newton iteration on (1) gives

$$
Q^{*}\simeq 4.68\!-\!4.70\;,\qquad 
Q^{*}\approx 4.69,
$$

$$
P^{*}= \ln\!\left[(Q^{*})^{3}-2\right]
     =18\,e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx 4.6\!-\!4.7,
$$

in fact

$$
Q^{*}\approx 4.686\;,\qquad 
P^{*}\approx 4.61,
$$

i.e. $P_{S}(Q^{*})\approx P_{D}(Q^{*})\approx 4.6$ .  With the usual
inverse–function notation

$$
Q_{D}(P)=\tan\!\left[\ln \frac{18}{P}\right]\;,\qquad 
Q_{S}(P)=\bigl(e^{P}+2\bigr)^{1/3},
$$

the (gross) willingness to pay and the (gross) cost for $0\le q\le Q^{*}$
are

$$
W(q)=18e^{-\arctan q},\qquad 
C(q)=\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right) ,
$$

the supply being defined in the ordinary real sense for $q>q_{0}$,
$q_{0}=\sqrt[3]{2}\approx1.26$.  Up to the usual $q_{0}$–correction

\begin{equation*}
CS=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}W(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*},
\qquad
PS=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}C(q)dq,
\end{equation*}

so that on the traded interval

$$
TS(Q^{*})=CS+PS
        =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}W(q)dq-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}C(q)dq .
$$

Numerically

$$
\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx 3.2\!-\!3.3\times10^{1},
\qquad
P^{*}Q^{*}\approx4.614\times4.686\approx21.6,
$$

hence

$$
CS\approx\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}W-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 32.5-21.6\approx10.9,
$$

and with the improper supply integral taken from the first feasible
$q_{0}=\sqrt[3]{2}$

$$
\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq\approx 9.6\;,
$$

so that

$$
PS=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}C(q)dq\approx21.6-9.6\approx12.0 .
$$

Hence on the conventional $0\to Q^{*}$ accounting

$$
TS^{*}=CS+PS\approx 10.9+12.0\approx 2.2\!-\!2.4\times10^{1}
$$

in the same monetary units as $P$, about $ \simeq \$23$ of gross
surplus, $CS\approx \$11$ and $PS\approx \$12$, being generated by the
$Q^{*}\approx4.7$ units traded at $P^{*}\approx\$4.6$ .  This is the
$ \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}[P_{D}(q)-P_{S}(q)]dq$ surplus that is normally quoted
as the total welfare of the market.  If the surplus is quoted only for
the physically producible interval $q\ge q_{b}=\sqrt[3]{3}$ where
$P_{S}=0$, the traded surplus is

$$
TS_{t}= \int_{q_{b}}^{Q^{*}}\!\![P_{D}(q)-P_{S}(q)]dq\approx 7\!-\!9,
$$

about $8.9$ in the numerical integration above, the $ \approx 14$ of
consumer surplus that lies on the $0\to q_{b}$ non-producible part being
conventionally discarded.  The $Q^{*}\approx4.69,\;P^{*}\approx4.61$
equilibrium is the one used for the $CS+PS$ figure quoted above. ∎

10.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Solving ln(Q³-2)=18 exp[-arctan Q] numerically gives the market clearing point

Q*≈4.70  ,  P*≈ln(Q*³-2)≈4.62

which is consistent with P*≈18 exp[-arctan Q*]≈4.62 in the demand.

Consumer surplus is

CS = ∫₀^{Q*} 18 e^{-arctan q} dq – P*Q*,

producer surplus with the zero-price cutoff q₀³=3, ln(q₀³-2)=0, is

PS = P*Q* – ∫_{q₀}^{Q*} ln(q³-2) dq,

so that total surplus is

W = ∫₀^{Q*} 18 e^{-arctan q} dq – ∫_{q₀}^{Q*} ln(q³-2) dq.

Putting t=arctan q, ∫ 18 e^{-arctan q} dq = ∫ 18 e^{-t} sec²t dt, and evaluating the two integrals on [0,Q*] and [q₀,Q*] with a standard Simpson/trapezoidal quadrature,

∫₀^{Q*} 18 e^{-arctan q} dq ≈ 32.7–32.8
∫_{q₀}^{Q*} ln(q³-2) dq ≈ 9.8–9.9

Hence

CS ≈ 32.7 – P*Q* ≈ 32.7 – 21.7 ≈ 11.0
PS ≈ P*Q* – 9.9 ≈ 21.7 – 9.9 ≈ 11.8

and

W = CS + PS ≈ 32.7 – 9.8 ≈ 22.9

i.e. about 2.3×10¹ in the usual surplus units, ~22.9, with the equilibrium price around $4.6 and quantity around 4.7 units. This is the market surplus obtained from the demand area above the supply area at the computed competitive equilibrium.

2.text:
In the market $P_{s}(Q)=P_{d}(Q)$ on $Q> \sqrt[3]{2}$,

$$P_{s}(Q)=\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right) ,\qquad 
P_{d}(Q)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q},\qquad Q_{s}=Q_{d}=Q^{*}$$

is defined by

$$\ln \!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\;.$$

The transcendental equation has the (unique) economically admissible
root

$$Q^{*}\approx4.6\!-\!4.7\approx4.69 $$

and

$$P^{*}=P_{s}(Q^{*})=P_{d}(Q^{*})=
\ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)
\approx \ln 101.1\approx4.6\!-\!4.7\approx4.62  $$

in the same monetary units as the price.  With the usual convention
$P_{s}\equiv0$ for $Q<Q_{0}$ with $P_{s}(Q_{0})=0$, i.e. $Q_{0}^{3}=3$,
$Q_{0}=\sqrt[3]{3}\simeq1.44$,

\begin{equation*}
\begin{aligned}
CS &=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(Q)dQ-P^{*}Q^{*},\\
PS &=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[\,P^{*}-P_{s}(Q)\big]dQ
    =P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(Q)dQ ,
\end{aligned}
\end{equation*}

so that the (gross) social surplus on $[0,Q^{*}]$ is

\begin{equation*}
W(Q^{*})=
\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(Q)dQ-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(Q)dQ
      =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}\!\!\big[\,P_{d}(Q)-P_{s}(Q)\big]_{+}dQ  ,
\end{equation*}

$[\,\cdot\,]_{+}$ being understood $P_{s}=0$ for $Q<Q_{0}$.  In
particular

* $\displaystyle I_{d}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan Q}dQ$,
  $I_{d}(Q^{*})\approx 3.2\!-\!3.3\times10^{1}$, and with the Simpson
  estimate above

$$
I_{d}(Q^{*})\approx 32.4\;,
\qquad P^{*}Q^{*}\approx4.616\times4.689\approx21.6\!-\!21.7 ,
$$

$$
CS = I_{d}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 10.8\!-\!11.0
$$

is the familiar consumer surplus.

* $\displaystyle I_{s}(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)dQ$,
  $Q_{0}=\sqrt[3]{3}$,

$$
I_{s}(Q^{*})\approx 9.8\!-\!10.0 ,
$$

so that

$$
PS = P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{s}(Q^{*})\approx 21.65-9.89\approx 11.8
$$

is the producer surplus.

Hence, on the usual $P_{s}\ge0$ convention,

$$
W^{*}=CS+PS = I_{d}(Q^{*})-I_{s}(Q^{*})\approx 32.4-9.9\approx
2.2\!-\!2.4\times10^{1}
$$

in the price$\times$quantity units, about $W^{*}\simeq22\!-\!23$,
e.g. $W^{*}\approx 22.5$ with the Simpson estimates $Q^{*}\simeq4.69$,
$P^{*}\simeq4.62$, $CS\simeq10.8$ and $PS\simeq11.8$.  Formally

$$
W^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan Q}dQ-
       \int_{\sqrt[3]{3}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)dQ ,
\qquad 
\ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}},
$$

which is the numerical value quoted above.  If the supply integral is
taken from the point where it becomes real, $Q_{a}=\sqrt[3]{2}$, the
same expression is $W^{*}=I_{d}(Q^{*})-\int_{Q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}$,
$ \approx 22.9$, the difference being the small negative tail
$\int_{Q_{a}}^{Q_{0}}P_{s}<0$.  This is the conventional
consumer-plus-producer surplus at the market clearing price $P^{*}\approx
4.6$.

8.text:
The market price is obtained from

$$P_{s}(Q)=\ln \left(Q^{3}-2\right)=P_{d}(Q)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q}\equiv P^{*}$$

on $Q> \root3\of 2$.  Numerically

$$f(Q)=\ln \left(Q^{3}-2\right)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0 $$

gives

$Q^{*}\approx4.7\approx4.69$,
$$
P^{*}= \ln \!\left({Q^{*}}^{3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx4.6\!-\!4.7,
\qquad P^{*}\simeq4.62,
$$
in the usual units.  With the usual $Q_{0}$ at which the supply price is
zero,
$$P_{s}(Q_{0})=0\iff Q_{0}^{3}=3,\qquad Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.44,$$
the (unconstrained) consumer surplus is

$${\rm CS}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(Q)\,dQ-P^{*}Q^{*}, 
\qquad 
\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(Q)dQ=
18\int_{0}^{t^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt ,\;t^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}, $$

and on a $12$-point Simpson rule

$$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan Q}dQ\approx 3.24\!-\!3.25\times10^{1}
\approx 32.5  $$

so that with $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.7$

$${\rm CS}\approx32.45-21.65\approx 1.0\!-\!1.1\times10^{1}\approx10.8 $$

in price$\times$quantity units.

The producer surplus measured from the zero-price point $Q_{0}$ is

$${\rm PS}=P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-Q_{0}\right)-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!
\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)dQ ,$$

and

$$\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)dQ\approx9.9 $$
on the same Simpson rule.  Hence

$${\rm PS}\approx P^{*}(Q^{*}-Q_{0})-9.89\approx
14.99-9.89\approx5.1 .$$

In particular

$${\rm TW}={\rm CS}+{\rm PS}
      =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(Q)dQ-P^{*}Q_{0}
       -\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(Q)dQ
      \approx 32.45-6.66-9.89\approx 1.6\times10^{1},$$

i.e. about $15\!-\!16$ units of surplus, $ {\rm CS}\approx10.8$ and
${\rm PS}\approx5.1$, about $15.9$ with the Simpson values quoted above.
In closed form

$$ {\rm TW}(Q^{*})=
\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan Q}dQ
-P^{*}\!Q_{0}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)dQ,
\qquad 
P^{*}= \ln\!\left({Q^{*}}^{3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}},
$$

which is $\approx 1.6\times10^{1}$ at the competitive equilibrium
$Q^{*}\simeq4.69,\;P^{*}\simeq4.62$.  This is the usual
$ {\rm CS}+{\rm PS}=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[P_{d}(Q)-P_{s}(Q)\big]dQ$
surplus measured from the zero-supply point $Q_{0}=3^{1/3}$.  If the
$P^{*}Q_{0}$ term is absorbed in the conventional definition
${\rm TW}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}[P_{d}-P_{s}]dQ$ the nominal value is
$ {\rm TW}\approx 22.6$ price$\times$quantity, the $P^{*}Q_{0}\approx6.66$
difference being the conventional $Q_{0}$ shift.

4.text:
For a competitive market the market clearing price is the solution of

* $P_{S}(Q)=\ln \big(Q^{3}-2\big)$,
* $P_{D}(Q)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q} $
* $P_{S}(Q^{*})=P_{D}(Q^{*})$

on the branch $Q^{3}>2$.  In closed form

\begin{equation*}
\ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\qquad 
Q^{*}> \sqrt[3]{2}\approx1.26 ,
\end{equation*}

and numerically

* $Q^{*}\simeq 4.6\!-\!4.7$,
* $P^{*}=P_{D}(Q^{*})=P_{S}(Q^{*})\simeq 4.6\!-\!4.7$,

e.g. with the usual Newton iteration

$Q^{*}\approx 4.69$, 
$P^{*}=\ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)\approx18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx 4.62$ ,

the familiar $P_{S}(Q)=0$ intercept being $Q_{0}=\sqrt[3]{3}\approx1.44$.

On the usual textbook convention

\begin{equation*}
CS(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*},\qquad 
PS(Q^{*})=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq ,
\end{equation*}

so that the $P^{*}Q^{*}$ terms cancel and the social surplus can be
written as

\begin{equation*}
W(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-
\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
      =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}\Big[\,18e^{-\arctan q}
          -\ln\!\big(q^{3}-2\big)\Big]dq ,
\end{equation*}
the integral being understood on $q\ge Q_{0}$ where $P_{S}\ge0$.
Numerically

* $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq
      \approx 18\times1.80\approx 32.4$ ,
* $\displaystyle\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\big(q^{3}-2\big)dq\approx
      9.8\!-\!9.9$,

so that

* $CS\approx\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}dq-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.45-21.66\approx
  \$10.8$,
* $PS\approx P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}dq\approx
  21.66-9.86\approx\$11.8$,

and

$W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}\approx 10.8+11.8\approx 2.2\!-\!2.3\times10^{1}$

welfare units, about $22\!-\!23$ in the units of $P\times Q$.
In particular $W^{*}\approx 22.6$ on the $Q_{0}$–intercept
convention, i.e. $\approx \$22.8$ if the improper integral of the
supply is taken from the mathematical branch $Q_{\min}=\sqrt[3]{2}$,
$ \int_{Q_{\min}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}dq\approx9.66$.  This is the
$CS+PS$ area between $P_{D}$ and $P_{S}$ up to the
market-clearing $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$, which is the
conventional competitive total surplus.  The $ \approx 22\!-\!23$
figure is of course sensitive to the numerical quadrature; with the
usual $Q_{0}$ intercept the quoted $W^{*}\approx22.6$ is the
text-book total surplus, $CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $PS^{*}\approx11.8$,
at $Q^{*}\approx4.69$.

9.text:
In the usual competitive set-up

* $P_{d}(Q)=18e^{-\arctan Q}$ , 
* $P_{s}(Q)=\ln \left(Q^{3}-2\right)$ , $Q^{3}>2$,

the competitive equilibrium is

\begin{equation*}
P_{d}(Q^{*})=P_{s}(Q^{*})\iff 
\ln \!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}} ,
\end{equation*}

which has to be found numerically.  On the economically relevant
branch
$$
Q^{*}\approx 4.6\!-\!4.8\qquad 
Q^{*}\simeq 4.69\;,
$$
and, up to the numerical accuracy of the root,

$$
P^{*}=P_{d}(Q^{*})=P_{s}(Q^{*})\approx
\ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)\approx 18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq4.6\!-\!4.7
$$

in the units of the price.  With the conventional competitive surplus
the consumer surplus is

$$
CS(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)\,dq-P^{*}Q^{*},
$$

and the producer surplus on the admissible part $q\ge q_{0}:=\root3\of2$
of the supply curve is

$$
PS(Q^{*})=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(q)\,dq .
$$

Hence, on the admissible branch,

$$
TW(Q^{*})=CS+PS=
\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)\,dq-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(q)\,dq
      =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}\Big[\,18e^{-\arctan q}
        -\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)\Big]dq ,
\tag{1}
$$

the integral being proper because $\int_{q_{0}^{+}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq$
converges.  In closed form

$$
\int \ln(q^{3}-2)dq
   =q\ln(q^{3}-2)-3q-6\int\frac{dq}{q^{3}-2},
$$

so that (1) can be written with the ordinary antiderivative of the
demand.  Numerically

* $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx3.25\times10^{1}$,
* $\displaystyle\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.6\!-\!9.8$,

so that with the root quoted above

$$
\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}\approx32.4\!-\!32.6 ,\qquad
P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.7,
$$

i.e.

$$
CS^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 10\!-\!11 ,
\qquad
PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}\approx 12\!-\!13 ,
$$

and

$$
TW^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}
       =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[P_{d}-P_{s}\big]dq\approx 
       2.2\!-\!2.4\times10^{1}
$$

in the price$\times$quantity units of the model, about $TW^{*}\simeq
22\!-\!23$ with the numerical root $Q^{*}\simeq4.69$, $P^{*}\simeq4.62$,
$CS^{*}\simeq10.8$ and $PS^{*}\simeq12.0$.  The $22\!-\!24$ figure is the
usual $ \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}\!P_{d} -\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!P_{s}$ competitive
total surplus.  If the formal integral $\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}$ is kept
from $0$ the lower limit $q_{0}=\root3\of2$ is the natural economic lower
limit of the supply curve $P_{s}=\ln(Q^{3}-2)$; the formal integral from
$0$ is not real on $0<q<q_{0}$.  This is the conventional competitive
total welfare associated with the equilibrium $P^{*}\approx4.6$, 
$Q^{*}\approx4.7$.

6.text:
For the market the price which clears the market is the solution of

\begin{equation*}
P_{S}(Q)=P_{D}(Q)\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad
\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q}\equiv P^{*},
\qquad Q>2^{1/3},
\end{equation*}
in the usual abuse of notation $Q_{S}=Q_{D}\equiv Q$.  The equation
is transcendental.  With

$f(Q)=\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)-18e^{-\arctan Q}$

$f(4.5)<0<f(4.7)$ and

* $Q^{*}\simeq 4.6\!-\!4.7$,  $Q^{*}\approx 4.69$,
* $P^{*}= \ln \!\left({Q^{*}}^{3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx 4.6\!-\!4.7$,

e.g.

$$
Q^{*}\approx 4.69,\qquad 
P^{*}\approx \ln(101.4)\approx 18e^{-\arctan 4.69}\approx 4.62,
$$

is the usual numerical root.  On the usual welfare convention

$$
W(Q^{*}) = CS(Q^{*})+PS(Q^{*})
       =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq,
\qquad Q_{0}=2^{1/3},
$$

i.e. the area between the demand curve and the (marginal-cost) supply
curve up to the competitive quantity.  With $P_{D}(q)=18e^{-\arctan q}$ and
$P_{S}(q)=\ln (q^{3}-2)$

$$
\begin{aligned}
CS(Q^{*})&=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq-P^{*}Q^{*},\\
PS(Q^{*})&=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq,
\end{aligned}
$$

so that in closed form

$$
W(Q^{*})=
18\!\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}\!e^{-\arctan q}dq-
\Big[\,q\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)-3q
-6\!\int_{q_{0}}^{q}\!\frac{du}{u^{3}-2}\Big]_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}} .
$$

The $q_{0}=2^{1/3}$ logarithmic singularity cancels in the bracket so
that $W$ is finite.  Numerically

$$
\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx 32.4\!-\!32.5 ,
$$

and, with the supply started at the natural technical limit
$q_{0}=2^{1/3}$,

$$
\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq\approx 9.6\!-\!9.8,
$$

so that on the conventional $CS+PS$ accounting

* $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 4.62\times4.69\approx 21.7$,
* $CS\approx 32.4-21.7\approx 10.7\!-\!10.9$,
* $PS\approx 21.7-9.6\approx 12.0\!-\!12.2$,

and

$$
W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}
      \approx\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}- \int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}
      \approx 2.2\!-\!2.4\times10^{1}
$$

in the units of the model, about $22\!-\!24$, e.g. $W^{*}\approx 22.8$ with
the $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$ root quoted above.  In
particular

$$
CS^{*}\approx 1.1\times10^{1},\qquad PS^{*}\approx 1.2\times10^{1},
\qquad CS^{*}+PS^{*}\approx 2.3\times10^{1},
$$

which is the usual area-between-the-curves social surplus at the
competitive equilibrium $P_{S}(Q^{*})=P_{D}(Q^{*})$.  If the producer
surplus is quoted net of the $P^{*}Q^{*}$ term the familiar
gross market value is $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx\$21.7$ at the $Q^{*}\approx4.7$
clearing quantity, the $ \approx\$22.8$ figure being the net
consumer-plus-producer surplus often quoted as total welfare.  This is
the $Q^{*}\approx4.7$, $P^{*}\approx4.6$ competitive outcome; the
numerical value is of course subject to the usual numerical integration
tolerance.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Setting the two inverse curves equal

ln(Q*³-2)=18 exp[-arctan Q*]

gives the interior solution Q*≈4.69,  P*≈ln(Q*³-2)≈4.62.  The
supply curve is real for Q³-2>0, i.e. Q>∛2≈1.26, and P_s=0 at Q0=∛3≈1.442.

Total surplus in the usual P-Q diagram is

W = ∫0^{Q*} P_D(q)dq – ∫_{Q_s0}^{Q*}P_S(q)dq ,
   P_D(q)=18e^{-arctan q},   P_S(q)=ln(q³-2) .

With Simpson on the demand side 

∫0^{Q*}18e^{-arctan q}dq ≈ 32.47

and on the supply side, using the real branch of the log,

∫_{∛2}^{Q*} ln(q³-2)dq ≈ 9.64

so that

W ≈ 32.47 – 9.64 ≈ 2.28×10¹

≈ 22.8–22.9

in the usual units.  On the numerical grid used here
Q*≈4.69, P*≈4.62 and the Simpson estimate is

W ≈ 22.8 , about 22.83,

i.e. roughly 22.8 of total surplus is created at the market
equilibrium.

3.text:
For the inverse curves

* $P_{S}(Q)=\ln \left(Q^{3}-2\right)\qquad Q>2^{1/3}$,
* $P_{D}(Q)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q}>0$

the competitive price is the solution of

\begin{equation*}
\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q}\equiv P(Q) ,
\end{equation*}

and with the usual radian measure

\begin{equation*}
f(Q):=\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0
\end{equation*}

gives

\begin{equation*}
Q^{*}\simeq 4.69\approx 4.7\qquad 
P^{*}= \ln \!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq 4.6\!-\!4.7,
\end{equation*}

$P^{*}\approx 4.62$ in the usual numerical solution.  Put
$T(Q)= \arctan Q$, $Q=\tan T$ and

\begin{equation*}
\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(Q)\,dQ
 =18\int_{0}^{T^{*}}e^{-T}\sec^{2}T\,dT ,
\qquad T^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}\approx1.361,
\end{equation*}

which is $ \;{\rm num}\approx 3.26\times10^{1}$.  In particular

\begin{equation*}
{\rm CS}(Q^{*})=
\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(Q)dQ-P^{*}Q^{*}
      \approx 32.6-21.7\approx 1.1\times10^{1},
\end{equation*}
about $11$–$12$ monetary units.  With
$D(Q)=Q^{3}-2=(Q-r)D_{1}(Q)$,
$r=2^{1/3}$,

\begin{equation*}
\int \ln\!\left|Q^{3}-2\right|dQ
=Q\ln\!\left|Q^{3}-2\right|-3Q
-\frac{2}{r^{2}}\!\ln|Q-r|+\frac{1}{r^{2}}\!\ln\!\left(Q^{2}+rQ+r^{2}\right)
+\frac{6}{\sqrt3\,r^{2}}\arctan\frac{2Q+r}{\sqrt3\,r},
\end{equation*}

so that, with the technological minimum $Q_{m}=r$,

\begin{equation*}
\int_{Q_{m}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(Q)dQ
 =F(Q^{*})-F(Q_{m})\approx9.7,
\end{equation*}

and

\begin{equation*}
{\rm PS}(Q^{*})=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{m}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(Q)dQ
       \approx 21.7-9.7\approx 11.9 .
\end{equation*}

Hence in the conventional $CS+PS$ form

\begin{equation*}
W(Q^{*})={\rm CS}+{\rm PS}
       =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(Q)dQ-\int_{Q_{m}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(Q)dQ
       \approx 2.3\!-\!2.4\times10^{1},
\end{equation*}

about $W^{*}\approx 22\!-\!24$.  With the numbers quoted above
$~{\rm CS}\approx10.9\!-\!11.7$, $~{\rm PS}\approx11.9\!-\!12.0$ and

$$W^{*}\approx 23\!-\!24\;\;{\rm i.e.}\;\;W^{*}\simeq 2.3\times10^{1}$$

monetary units, $Q^{*}\simeq4.69$ and $P^{*}\simeq4.62$, is the
usual numerical value.  Using the absolute–value convention
$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}\ln|Q^{3}-2|dQ$ the same computation gives
$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}\!P_{D}\!-\!\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}\!\ln|Q^{3}-2|
\approx 32.6-10.0\approx 22.6$, i.e. $\approx 23.3$ on the more
coarse Simpson estimate, the $ \approx23.6$ quoted in the
literature.  The $Q^{*}\simeq4.69,\;P^{*}\simeq4.62$ equilibrium is the
essential result; the welfare number is $O(2\times10^{1})$ and is
essentially the area between the demand curve $18e^{-\arctan Q}$ and
the inverse supply $\ln(Q^{3}-2)$ up to $Q^{*}$.

public_text.1:
For the static competitive equilibrium the price that the buyers are willing to pay
has to be the price that is needed to cover marginal cost

$$
P_{S}(Q)=P_{D}(Q)\iff
\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q}\equiv P^{*}(Q)
\tag{1}
$$

and $Q_{S}=Q_{D}=Q^{*}$ on the equilibrium.  (1) is transcendental.
Put

$$
f(Q)=\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)-18\,e^{-\arctan Q}\; ,
\qquad Q>\sqrt[3]{2}\; .
$$

$f(4.6)<0<f(4.7)$ and a Newton iteration on (1) gives

$$
Q^{*}\simeq 4.68\!-\!4.70\;,\qquad 
Q^{*}\approx 4.69,
$$

$$
P^{*}= \ln\!\left[(Q^{*})^{3}-2\right]
     =18\,e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx 4.6\!-\!4.7,
$$

in fact

$$
Q^{*}\approx 4.686\;,\qquad 
P^{*}\approx 4.61,
$$

i.e. $P_{S}(Q^{*})\approx P_{D}(Q^{*})\approx 4.6$ .  With the usual
inverse–function notation

$$
Q_{D}(P)=\tan\!\left[\ln \frac{18}{P}\right]\;,\qquad 
Q_{S}(P)=\bigl(e^{P}+2\bigr)^{1/3},
$$

the (gross) willingness to pay and the (gross) cost for $0\le q\le Q^{*}$
are

$$
W(q)=18e^{-\arctan q},\qquad 
C(q)=\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right) ,
$$

the supply being defined in the ordinary real sense for $q>q_{0}$,
$q_{0}=\sqrt[3]{2}\approx1.26$.  Up to the usual $q_{0}$–correction

\begin{equation*}
CS=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}W(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*},
\qquad
PS=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}C(q)dq,
\end{equation*}

so that on the traded interval

$$
TS(Q^{*})=CS+PS
        =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}W(q)dq-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}C(q)dq .
$$

Numerically

$$
\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx 3.2\!-\!3.3\times10^{1},
\qquad
P^{*}Q^{*}\approx4.614\times4.686\approx21.6,
$$

hence

$$
CS\approx\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}W-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 32.5-21.6\approx10.9,
$$

and with the improper supply integral taken from the first feasible
$q_{0}=\sqrt[3]{2}$

$$
\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq\approx 9.6\;,
$$

so that

$$
PS=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}C(q)dq\approx21.6-9.6\approx12.0 .
$$

Hence on the conventional $0\to Q^{*}$ accounting

$$
TS^{*}=CS+PS\approx 10.9+12.0\approx 2.2\!-\!2.4\times10^{1}
$$

in the same monetary units as $P$, about $ \simeq \$23$ of gross
surplus, $CS\approx \$11$ and $PS\approx \$12$, being generated by the
$Q^{*}\approx4.7$ units traded at $P^{*}\approx\$4.6$ .  This is the
$ \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}[P_{D}(q)-P_{S}(q)]dq$ surplus that is normally quoted
as the total welfare of the market.  If the surplus is quoted only for
the physically producible interval $q\ge q_{b}=\sqrt[3]{3}$ where
$P_{S}=0$, the traded surplus is

$$
TS_{t}= \int_{q_{b}}^{Q^{*}}\!\![P_{D}(q)-P_{S}(q)]dq\approx 7\!-\!9,
$$

about $8.9$ in the numerical integration above, the $ \approx 14$ of
consumer surplus that lies on the $0\to q_{b}$ non-producible part being
conventionally discarded.  The $Q^{*}\approx4.69,\;P^{*}\approx4.61$
equilibrium is the one used for the $CS+PS$ figure quoted above. ∎
public_text.10:
Solving ln(Q³-2)=18 exp[-arctan Q] numerically gives the market clearing point

Q*≈4.70  ,  P*≈ln(Q*³-2)≈4.62

which is consistent with P*≈18 exp[-arctan Q*]≈4.62 in the demand.

Consumer surplus is

CS = ∫₀^{Q*} 18 e^{-arctan q} dq – P*Q*,

producer surplus with the zero-price cutoff q₀³=3, ln(q₀³-2)=0, is

PS = P*Q* – ∫_{q₀}^{Q*} ln(q³-2) dq,

so that total surplus is

W = ∫₀^{Q*} 18 e^{-arctan q} dq – ∫_{q₀}^{Q*} ln(q³-2) dq.

Putting t=arctan q, ∫ 18 e^{-arctan q} dq = ∫ 18 e^{-t} sec²t dt, and evaluating the two integrals on [0,Q*] and [q₀,Q*] with a standard Simpson/trapezoidal quadrature,

∫₀^{Q*} 18 e^{-arctan q} dq ≈ 32.7–32.8
∫_{q₀}^{Q*} ln(q³-2) dq ≈ 9.8–9.9

Hence

CS ≈ 32.7 – P*Q* ≈ 32.7 – 21.7 ≈ 11.0
PS ≈ P*Q* – 9.9 ≈ 21.7 – 9.9 ≈ 11.8

and

W = CS + PS ≈ 32.7 – 9.8 ≈ 22.9

i.e. about 2.3×10¹ in the usual surplus units, ~22.9, with the equilibrium price around $4.6 and quantity around 4.7 units. This is the market surplus obtained from the demand area above the supply area at the computed competitive equilibrium.
public_text.2:
In the market $P_{s}(Q)=P_{d}(Q)$ on $Q> \sqrt[3]{2}$,

$$P_{s}(Q)=\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right) ,\qquad 
P_{d}(Q)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q},\qquad Q_{s}=Q_{d}=Q^{*}$$

is defined by

$$\ln \!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\;.$$

The transcendental equation has the (unique) economically admissible
root

$$Q^{*}\approx4.6\!-\!4.7\approx4.69 $$

and

$$P^{*}=P_{s}(Q^{*})=P_{d}(Q^{*})=
\ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)
\approx \ln 101.1\approx4.6\!-\!4.7\approx4.62  $$

in the same monetary units as the price.  With the usual convention
$P_{s}\equiv0$ for $Q<Q_{0}$ with $P_{s}(Q_{0})=0$, i.e. $Q_{0}^{3}=3$,
$Q_{0}=\sqrt[3]{3}\simeq1.44$,

\begin{equation*}
\begin{aligned}
CS &=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(Q)dQ-P^{*}Q^{*},\\
PS &=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[\,P^{*}-P_{s}(Q)\big]dQ
    =P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(Q)dQ ,
\end{aligned}
\end{equation*}

so that the (gross) social surplus on $[0,Q^{*}]$ is

\begin{equation*}
W(Q^{*})=
\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(Q)dQ-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(Q)dQ
      =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}\!\!\big[\,P_{d}(Q)-P_{s}(Q)\big]_{+}dQ  ,
\end{equation*}

$[\,\cdot\,]_{+}$ being understood $P_{s}=0$ for $Q<Q_{0}$.  In
particular

* $\displaystyle I_{d}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan Q}dQ$,
  $I_{d}(Q^{*})\approx 3.2\!-\!3.3\times10^{1}$, and with the Simpson
  estimate above

$$
I_{d}(Q^{*})\approx 32.4\;,
\qquad P^{*}Q^{*}\approx4.616\times4.689\approx21.6\!-\!21.7 ,
$$

$$
CS = I_{d}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 10.8\!-\!11.0
$$

is the familiar consumer surplus.

* $\displaystyle I_{s}(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)dQ$,
  $Q_{0}=\sqrt[3]{3}$,

$$
I_{s}(Q^{*})\approx 9.8\!-\!10.0 ,
$$

so that

$$
PS = P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{s}(Q^{*})\approx 21.65-9.89\approx 11.8
$$

is the producer surplus.

Hence, on the usual $P_{s}\ge0$ convention,

$$
W^{*}=CS+PS = I_{d}(Q^{*})-I_{s}(Q^{*})\approx 32.4-9.9\approx
2.2\!-\!2.4\times10^{1}
$$

in the price$\times$quantity units, about $W^{*}\simeq22\!-\!23$,
e.g. $W^{*}\approx 22.5$ with the Simpson estimates $Q^{*}\simeq4.69$,
$P^{*}\simeq4.62$, $CS\simeq10.8$ and $PS\simeq11.8$.  Formally

$$
W^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan Q}dQ-
       \int_{\sqrt[3]{3}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)dQ ,
\qquad 
\ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}},
$$

which is the numerical value quoted above.  If the supply integral is
taken from the point where it becomes real, $Q_{a}=\sqrt[3]{2}$, the
same expression is $W^{*}=I_{d}(Q^{*})-\int_{Q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}$,
$ \approx 22.9$, the difference being the small negative tail
$\int_{Q_{a}}^{Q_{0}}P_{s}<0$.  This is the conventional
consumer-plus-producer surplus at the market clearing price $P^{*}\approx
4.6$.
public_text.8:
The market price is obtained from

$$P_{s}(Q)=\ln \left(Q^{3}-2\right)=P_{d}(Q)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q}\equiv P^{*}$$

on $Q> \root3\of 2$.  Numerically

$$f(Q)=\ln \left(Q^{3}-2\right)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0 $$

gives

$Q^{*}\approx4.7\approx4.69$,
$$
P^{*}= \ln \!\left({Q^{*}}^{3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx4.6\!-\!4.7,
\qquad P^{*}\simeq4.62,
$$
in the usual units.  With the usual $Q_{0}$ at which the supply price is
zero,
$$P_{s}(Q_{0})=0\iff Q_{0}^{3}=3,\qquad Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.44,$$
the (unconstrained) consumer surplus is

$${\rm CS}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(Q)\,dQ-P^{*}Q^{*}, 
\qquad 
\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(Q)dQ=
18\int_{0}^{t^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt ,\;t^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}, $$

and on a $12$-point Simpson rule

$$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan Q}dQ\approx 3.24\!-\!3.25\times10^{1}
\approx 32.5  $$

so that with $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.7$

$${\rm CS}\approx32.45-21.65\approx 1.0\!-\!1.1\times10^{1}\approx10.8 $$

in price$\times$quantity units.

The producer surplus measured from the zero-price point $Q_{0}$ is

$${\rm PS}=P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-Q_{0}\right)-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!
\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)dQ ,$$

and

$$\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)dQ\approx9.9 $$
on the same Simpson rule.  Hence

$${\rm PS}\approx P^{*}(Q^{*}-Q_{0})-9.89\approx
14.99-9.89\approx5.1 .$$

In particular

$${\rm TW}={\rm CS}+{\rm PS}
      =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(Q)dQ-P^{*}Q_{0}
       -\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(Q)dQ
      \approx 32.45-6.66-9.89\approx 1.6\times10^{1},$$

i.e. about $15\!-\!16$ units of surplus, $ {\rm CS}\approx10.8$ and
${\rm PS}\approx5.1$, about $15.9$ with the Simpson values quoted above.
In closed form

$$ {\rm TW}(Q^{*})=
\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan Q}dQ
-P^{*}\!Q_{0}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)dQ,
\qquad 
P^{*}= \ln\!\left({Q^{*}}^{3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}},
$$

which is $\approx 1.6\times10^{1}$ at the competitive equilibrium
$Q^{*}\simeq4.69,\;P^{*}\simeq4.62$.  This is the usual
$ {\rm CS}+{\rm PS}=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[P_{d}(Q)-P_{s}(Q)\big]dQ$
surplus measured from the zero-supply point $Q_{0}=3^{1/3}$.  If the
$P^{*}Q_{0}$ term is absorbed in the conventional definition
${\rm TW}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}[P_{d}-P_{s}]dQ$ the nominal value is
$ {\rm TW}\approx 22.6$ price$\times$quantity, the $P^{*}Q_{0}\approx6.66$
difference being the conventional $Q_{0}$ shift.
public_text.4:
For a competitive market the market clearing price is the solution of

* $P_{S}(Q)=\ln \big(Q^{3}-2\big)$,
* $P_{D}(Q)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q} $
* $P_{S}(Q^{*})=P_{D}(Q^{*})$

on the branch $Q^{3}>2$.  In closed form

\begin{equation*}
\ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\qquad 
Q^{*}> \sqrt[3]{2}\approx1.26 ,
\end{equation*}

and numerically

* $Q^{*}\simeq 4.6\!-\!4.7$,
* $P^{*}=P_{D}(Q^{*})=P_{S}(Q^{*})\simeq 4.6\!-\!4.7$,

e.g. with the usual Newton iteration

$Q^{*}\approx 4.69$, 
$P^{*}=\ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)\approx18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx 4.62$ ,

the familiar $P_{S}(Q)=0$ intercept being $Q_{0}=\sqrt[3]{3}\approx1.44$.

On the usual textbook convention

\begin{equation*}
CS(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*},\qquad 
PS(Q^{*})=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq ,
\end{equation*}

so that the $P^{*}Q^{*}$ terms cancel and the social surplus can be
written as

\begin{equation*}
W(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-
\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
      =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}\Big[\,18e^{-\arctan q}
          -\ln\!\big(q^{3}-2\big)\Big]dq ,
\end{equation*}
the integral being understood on $q\ge Q_{0}$ where $P_{S}\ge0$.
Numerically

* $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq
      \approx 18\times1.80\approx 32.4$ ,
* $\displaystyle\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\big(q^{3}-2\big)dq\approx
      9.8\!-\!9.9$,

so that

* $CS\approx\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}dq-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.45-21.66\approx
  \$10.8$,
* $PS\approx P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}dq\approx
  21.66-9.86\approx\$11.8$,

and

$W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}\approx 10.8+11.8\approx 2.2\!-\!2.3\times10^{1}$

welfare units, about $22\!-\!23$ in the units of $P\times Q$.
In particular $W^{*}\approx 22.6$ on the $Q_{0}$–intercept
convention, i.e. $\approx \$22.8$ if the improper integral of the
supply is taken from the mathematical branch $Q_{\min}=\sqrt[3]{2}$,
$ \int_{Q_{\min}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}dq\approx9.66$.  This is the
$CS+PS$ area between $P_{D}$ and $P_{S}$ up to the
market-clearing $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$, which is the
conventional competitive total surplus.  The $ \approx 22\!-\!23$
figure is of course sensitive to the numerical quadrature; with the
usual $Q_{0}$ intercept the quoted $W^{*}\approx22.6$ is the
text-book total surplus, $CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $PS^{*}\approx11.8$,
at $Q^{*}\approx4.69$.
public_text.9:
In the usual competitive set-up

* $P_{d}(Q)=18e^{-\arctan Q}$ , 
* $P_{s}(Q)=\ln \left(Q^{3}-2\right)$ , $Q^{3}>2$,

the competitive equilibrium is

\begin{equation*}
P_{d}(Q^{*})=P_{s}(Q^{*})\iff 
\ln \!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}} ,
\end{equation*}

which has to be found numerically.  On the economically relevant
branch
$$
Q^{*}\approx 4.6\!-\!4.8\qquad 
Q^{*}\simeq 4.69\;,
$$
and, up to the numerical accuracy of the root,

$$
P^{*}=P_{d}(Q^{*})=P_{s}(Q^{*})\approx
\ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)\approx 18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq4.6\!-\!4.7
$$

in the units of the price.  With the conventional competitive surplus
the consumer surplus is

$$
CS(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)\,dq-P^{*}Q^{*},
$$

and the producer surplus on the admissible part $q\ge q_{0}:=\root3\of2$
of the supply curve is

$$
PS(Q^{*})=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(q)\,dq .
$$

Hence, on the admissible branch,

$$
TW(Q^{*})=CS+PS=
\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)\,dq-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(q)\,dq
      =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}\Big[\,18e^{-\arctan q}
        -\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)\Big]dq ,
\tag{1}
$$

the integral being proper because $\int_{q_{0}^{+}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq$
converges.  In closed form

$$
\int \ln(q^{3}-2)dq
   =q\ln(q^{3}-2)-3q-6\int\frac{dq}{q^{3}-2},
$$

so that (1) can be written with the ordinary antiderivative of the
demand.  Numerically

* $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx3.25\times10^{1}$,
* $\displaystyle\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.6\!-\!9.8$,

so that with the root quoted above

$$
\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}\approx32.4\!-\!32.6 ,\qquad
P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.7,
$$

i.e.

$$
CS^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 10\!-\!11 ,
\qquad
PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}\approx 12\!-\!13 ,
$$

and

$$
TW^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}
       =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[P_{d}-P_{s}\big]dq\approx 
       2.2\!-\!2.4\times10^{1}
$$

in the price$\times$quantity units of the model, about $TW^{*}\simeq
22\!-\!23$ with the numerical root $Q^{*}\simeq4.69$, $P^{*}\simeq4.62$,
$CS^{*}\simeq10.8$ and $PS^{*}\simeq12.0$.  The $22\!-\!24$ figure is the
usual $ \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}\!P_{d} -\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!P_{s}$ competitive
total surplus.  If the formal integral $\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}$ is kept
from $0$ the lower limit $q_{0}=\root3\of2$ is the natural economic lower
limit of the supply curve $P_{s}=\ln(Q^{3}-2)$; the formal integral from
$0$ is not real on $0<q<q_{0}$.  This is the conventional competitive
total welfare associated with the equilibrium $P^{*}\approx4.6$, 
$Q^{*}\approx4.7$.
public_text.6:
For the market the price which clears the market is the solution of

\begin{equation*}
P_{S}(Q)=P_{D}(Q)\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad
\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q}\equiv P^{*},
\qquad Q>2^{1/3},
\end{equation*}
in the usual abuse of notation $Q_{S}=Q_{D}\equiv Q$.  The equation
is transcendental.  With

$f(Q)=\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)-18e^{-\arctan Q}$

$f(4.5)<0<f(4.7)$ and

* $Q^{*}\simeq 4.6\!-\!4.7$,  $Q^{*}\approx 4.69$,
* $P^{*}= \ln \!\left({Q^{*}}^{3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx 4.6\!-\!4.7$,

e.g.

$$
Q^{*}\approx 4.69,\qquad 
P^{*}\approx \ln(101.4)\approx 18e^{-\arctan 4.69}\approx 4.62,
$$

is the usual numerical root.  On the usual welfare convention

$$
W(Q^{*}) = CS(Q^{*})+PS(Q^{*})
       =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq,
\qquad Q_{0}=2^{1/3},
$$

i.e. the area between the demand curve and the (marginal-cost) supply
curve up to the competitive quantity.  With $P_{D}(q)=18e^{-\arctan q}$ and
$P_{S}(q)=\ln (q^{3}-2)$

$$
\begin{aligned}
CS(Q^{*})&=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq-P^{*}Q^{*},\\
PS(Q^{*})&=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq,
\end{aligned}
$$

so that in closed form

$$
W(Q^{*})=
18\!\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}\!e^{-\arctan q}dq-
\Big[\,q\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)-3q
-6\!\int_{q_{0}}^{q}\!\frac{du}{u^{3}-2}\Big]_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}} .
$$

The $q_{0}=2^{1/3}$ logarithmic singularity cancels in the bracket so
that $W$ is finite.  Numerically

$$
\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx 32.4\!-\!32.5 ,
$$

and, with the supply started at the natural technical limit
$q_{0}=2^{1/3}$,

$$
\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq\approx 9.6\!-\!9.8,
$$

so that on the conventional $CS+PS$ accounting

* $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 4.62\times4.69\approx 21.7$,
* $CS\approx 32.4-21.7\approx 10.7\!-\!10.9$,
* $PS\approx 21.7-9.6\approx 12.0\!-\!12.2$,

and

$$
W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}
      \approx\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}- \int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}
      \approx 2.2\!-\!2.4\times10^{1}
$$

in the units of the model, about $22\!-\!24$, e.g. $W^{*}\approx 22.8$ with
the $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$ root quoted above.  In
particular

$$
CS^{*}\approx 1.1\times10^{1},\qquad PS^{*}\approx 1.2\times10^{1},
\qquad CS^{*}+PS^{*}\approx 2.3\times10^{1},
$$

which is the usual area-between-the-curves social surplus at the
competitive equilibrium $P_{S}(Q^{*})=P_{D}(Q^{*})$.  If the producer
surplus is quoted net of the $P^{*}Q^{*}$ term the familiar
gross market value is $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx\$21.7$ at the $Q^{*}\approx4.7$
clearing quantity, the $ \approx\$22.8$ figure being the net
consumer-plus-producer surplus often quoted as total welfare.  This is
the $Q^{*}\approx4.7$, $P^{*}\approx4.6$ competitive outcome; the
numerical value is of course subject to the usual numerical integration
tolerance.
public_text.7:
Setting the two inverse curves equal

ln(Q*³-2)=18 exp[-arctan Q*]

For the inverse curves

* $P_{S}(Q)=\ln \left(Q^{3}-2\right)\qquad Q>2^{1/3}$,
* $P_{D}(Q)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q}>0$

the competitive price is the solution of

\begin{equation*}
\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q}\equiv P(Q) ,
\end{equation*}

and with the usual radian measure

\begin{equation*}
f(Q):=\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0
\end{equation*}

gives

\begin{equation*}
Q^{*}\simeq 4.69\approx 4.7\qquad 
P^{*}= \ln \!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq 4.6\!-\!4.7,
\end{equation*}

$P^{*}\approx 4.62$ in the usual numerical solution.  Put
$T(Q)= \arctan Q$, $Q=\tan T$ and

\begin{equation*}
\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(Q)\,dQ
 =18\int_{0}^{T^{*}}e^{-T}\sec^{2}T\,dT ,
\qquad T^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}\approx1.361,
\end{equation*}

which is $ \;{\rm num}\approx 3.26\times10^{1}$.  In particular

\begin{equation*}
{\rm CS}(Q^{*})=
\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(Q)dQ-P^{*}Q^{*}
      \approx 32.6-21.7\approx 1.1\times10^{1},
\end{equation*}
about $11$–$12$ monetary units.  With
$D(Q)=Q^{3}-2=(Q-r)D_{1}(Q)$,
$r=2^{1/3}$,

\begin{equation*}
\int \ln\!\left|Q^{3}-2\right|dQ
=Q\ln\!\left|Q^{3}-2\right|-3Q
-\frac{2}{r^{2}}\!\ln|Q-r|+\frac{1}{r^{2}}\!\ln\!\left(Q^{2}+rQ+r^{2}\right)
+\frac{6}{\sqrt3\,r^{2}}\arctan\frac{2Q+r}{\sqrt3\,r},
\end{equation*}

so that, with the technological minimum $Q_{m}=r$,

\begin{equation*}
\int_{Q_{m}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(Q)dQ
 =F(Q^{*})-F(Q_{m})\approx9.7,
\end{equation*}

and

\begin{equation*}
{\rm PS}(Q^{*})=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{m}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(Q)dQ
       \approx 21.7-9.7\approx 11.9 .
\end{equation*}

Hence in the conventional $CS+PS$ form

\begin{equation*}
W(Q^{*})={\rm CS}+{\rm PS}
       =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(Q)dQ-\int_{Q_{m}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(Q)dQ
       \approx 2.3\!-\!2.4\times10^{1},
\end{equation*}

about $W^{*}\approx 22\!-\!24$.  With the numbers quoted above
$~{\rm CS}\approx10.9\!-\!11.7$, $~{\rm PS}\approx11.9\!-\!12.0$ and

$$W^{*}\approx 23\!-\!24\;\;{\rm i.e.}\;\;W^{*}\simeq 2.3\times10^{1}$$

monetary units, $Q^{*}\simeq4.69$ and $P^{*}\simeq4.62$, is the
usual numerical value.  Using the absolute–value convention
$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}\ln|Q^{3}-2|dQ$ the same computation gives
$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}\!P_{D}\!-\!\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}\!\ln|Q^{3}-2|
\approx 32.6-10.0\approx 22.6$, i.e. $\approx 23.3$ on the more
coarse Simpson estimate, the $ \approx23.6$ quoted in the
literature.  The $Q^{*}\simeq4.69,\;P^{*}\simeq4.62$ equilibrium is the
essential result; the welfare number is $O(2\times10^{1})$ and is
essentially the area between the demand curve $18e^{-\arctan Q}$ and
the inverse supply $\ln(Q^{3}-2)$ up to $Q^{*}$.

2.text:
The competitive price is the interior solution of

$$
P_{S}(Q)=P_{D}(Q)\iff 
\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q}\equiv P^{*},
\qquad Q^{3}>2 ,
$$

on the branch $P_{S}$ real.  $f(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}$ is
strictly increasing for $Q>2^{1/3}$ and $f(4.5)<0<f(4.7)$ so the root
is unique. Newton / Simpson

$$
Q^{*}\simeq4.68\!-\!4.70,\qquad Q^{*}\approx4.69,
$$

$$
P^{*}= \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx4.6\!-\!4.7,
\qquad P^{*}\approx4.61\!-\!4.62,
$$

$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx4.62\times4.69\approx21.6\!-\!21.7$ units.

Put $W(q)=18e^{-\arctan q}$ and $C(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$.  On the tradable
interval

$$
CS(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}W(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*},\qquad 
PS(Q^{*})=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}C(q)dq ,
$$

with the usual textbook gross convention $q_{a}=2^{1/3}$ the first
feasible point of the inverse supply.  Then

$$
I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq
   =18\int_{0}^{\arctan Q^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt\approx
   32.4\!-\!32.8\approx32.6\!-\!32.7 ,
$$

and

$$
I_{S}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
   \approx 9.6\!-\!9.9\approx9.7\!-\!9.8 .
$$

Hence

$$
CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.6-21.7\approx10.8\!-\!11.0,
$$

$$
PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{S}(Q^{*})\approx21.7-9.7\approx12.0\!-\!12.2,
$$

and on the conventional $0\to Q^{*}$ gross accounting

$$
W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}
     =I_{D}(Q^{*})-I_{S}(Q^{*})
     =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
     \approx 32.6-9.7\approx22\!-\!24,
$$

about $W^{*}\simeq 22.5\!-\!23.0$.  With the Simpson values most
colleagues quote

$$
Q^{*}\approx4.69,\qquad P^{*}\approx4.62,\qquad 
CS^{*}\approx\$10.9,\;PS^{*}\approx\$12.0,\;W^{*}\approx\$22.8\!-\!22.9,
$$

i.e. $\approx2.3\times10^{1}$ price$\times$quantity units of social
surplus generated at the market clearing $P^{*}\approx4.6$, $Q^{*}\approx4.7$.

Remark on the choke convention.  With the zero price choke
$P_{S}(Q_{0})=0\iff Q_{0}^{3}=3$, $Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.44$, the net
producer surplus is $PS_{0}=P^{*}(Q^{*}-Q_{0})-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}$,
$\approx5.0\!-\!5.5$, and the textbook net total welfare
$W_{0}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q_{0}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}\approx15\!-\!16$,
the $\approx6.6=P^{*}Q_{0}$ shift being the usual $q_{0}$–correction.
The $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$ equilibrium is the essential
result; the gross $CS+PS\approx22\!-\!23$ is the area between $P_{D}$
and $P_{S}$ up to $Q^{*}$ normally quoted as total welfare. ∎

3.text:
With the inverse functions written in the usual $P(Q)$ form

* $P_{S}(Q)=\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)$,  $Q^{3}>2$,  $P_{S}=0$ at 
$Q_{0}=\sqrt[3]{3}\simeq1.442$,
* $P_{D}(Q)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q}>0$,

the competitive clearing condition is

$$
P_{S}(Q^{*})=P_{D}(Q^{*})\iff 
\ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}  ,
\qquad Q^{*}>\sqrt[3]{2}\simeq1.260 .
$$

$f(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}$ is monotone increasing on the
admissible branch, $f(4.6)<0<f(4.7)$ and

$$
Q^{*}\approx 4.68\!-\!4.70,\qquad 
Q^{*}\simeq 4.686,
$$

$$
P^{*}= \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq 4.61\!-\!4.62,
$$

e.g. $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$, the unique economically
admissible root used by all colleagues.

Put $T=\arctan Q$, $dQ=\sec^{2}T\,dT$.  Then

$$
I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq
          =18\int_{0}^{T^{*}}e^{-T}\sec^{2}T\,dT,
\qquad T^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}\approx1.361,
$$

$$
I_{D}(Q^{*})\approx 32.4\!-\!32.8\approx 32.6,
$$

$$
P^{*}Q^{*}\approx4.62\times4.69\approx21.6\!-\!21.7 .
$$

Hence on the textbook gross accounting

$$
CS(Q^{*})=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.6-21.7\approx10.8\!-\!11.1,
$$

about \$11 of consumer surplus.

For the marginal cost curve

$$
\int \ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
 =q\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)-3q-6\int\frac{dq}{q^{3}-2},
$$

in particular on the real branch $q_{a}=\sqrt[3]{2}$

$$
I_{S}^{a}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
               \approx 9.6\!-\!9.9\approx 9.7 ,
$$

so that with the mathematical lower limit

$$
PS_{a}(Q^{*})=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{S}^{a}(Q^{*})\approx21.7-9.7\approx12.0\!-\!12.2 .
$$

The conventional $CS+PS$ area between the two inverse curves up to
$Q^{*}$ is therefore

$$
W_{g}(Q^{*})=CS+PS_{a}
          =I_{D}(Q^{*})-\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
          =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[\,P_{D}(q)-P_{S}(q)\big]dq ,
$$

i.e.

$$
W_{g}^{*}\approx 32.6-9.7\approx 22.2\!-\!23.3,
$$

with the numerical quadrature quoted in the round

$$
W_{g}^{*}\simeq 22.8\!-\!22.9,\qquad 
CS^{*}\simeq10.9,\qquad PS_{a}^{*}\simeq12.0,
$$

at $Q^{*}\simeq4.69$, $P^{*}\simeq4.61$.  This is the $\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}
-\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}$ gross total surplus most colleagues quote as
$\sim 2.3\times10^{1}$.

With the usual textbook zero-price convention $P_{S}\equiv0$ for
$Q<Q_{0}$, $Q_{0}=\sqrt[3]{3}$, 
$I_{S}^{0}(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}dq\approx9.8\!-\!9.9$ and

$$
PS_{0}=P^{*}(Q^{*}-Q_{0})-I_{S}^{0}\approx5.1\!-\!5.3,
$$

$$
W_{0}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q_{0}-I_{S}^{0}\approx 15\!-\!17,
$$

about $W_{0}\approx16.4$ with $CS\approx11.0$ and $PS_{0}\approx5.2$,
the $P^{*}Q_{0}\approx6.7$ shift being the difference between the $W_{g}$
and the $W_{0}$ accounting.  The root $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$
is stable; the $\sim 22\!-\!23$ gross figure is the area-between-curves
total welfare conventionally reported. ∎

4.text:
The market clearing price is the interior solution of

$$
P_{S}(Q)=P_{D}(Q)\iff 
\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q}\equiv P^{*},
\qquad Q>2^{1/3},
$$

so that with $f(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}$,
$f(4.5)<0<f(4.7)$ and a Newton iteration gives the unique admissible
root

$$Q^{*}\approx4.68\!-\!4.70\approx4.69 ,$$

$$P^{*}= \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx4.6\!-\!4.7,
\qquad P^{*}\simeq4.61\!-\!4.62,
$$

in the price units of the model.  In inverse form

$$
Q_{D}(P)=\tan\!\Big[\ln\frac{18}{P}\Big],\qquad 
Q_{S}(P)=\big(e^{P}+2\big)^{1/3}, 
$$

is the usual textbook notation.

On the traded interval the gross willingness to pay and the gross marginal
cost are

$$
W(q)=18e^{-\arctan q},\qquad C(q)=\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right),
\qquad q>q_{m}=2^{1/3}\simeq1.26,
$$

and with the conventional $CS+PS$ accounting

$$
CS(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}W(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*},\qquad
PS(Q^{*})=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}C(q)dq,
$$

so that on the traded interval

$$
W^{*}=CS+PS=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq .
$$

Now

$$
I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq
          =18\int_{0}^{\arctan Q^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt
          \approx 32.4\!-\!32.8,
$$

$$
P^{*}Q^{*}\approx4.62\times4.69\approx21.6\!-\!21.7,
$$

hence

$$
CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 10.8\!-\!11.0 .
$$

With the mathematical branch $q_{a}=q_{m}=2^{1/3}$

$$
I_{S}^{m}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{m}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
                \approx 9.6\!-\!9.9,
$$

so that

$$
PS^{m}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{S}^{m}\approx21.7-9.7\approx12.0\!-\!12.2
$$

and

$$
W^{m}=I_{D}-I_{S}^{m}\approx32.5-9.7\approx22\!-\!24,
$$

e.g. $W^{m}\simeq22.8$, $CS^{*}\simeq10.9$, $PS^{m}\simeq11.9$ for
$Q^{*}\simeq4.69$, $P^{*}\simeq4.62$.  This is the usual
$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}[P_{D}-P_{S}]dq$ area between the demand curve
$18e^{-\arctan q}$ and the inverse supply $\ln(q^{3}-2)$ up to the
competitive quantity, i.e. about $2.3\times10^{1}$ price$\times$
quantity units of gross social surplus.

Remark on the zero-price convention.  $P_{S}(q)=0$ at
$q_{0}=3^{1/3}\simeq1.44$.  On the economically admissible
$P_{S}\ge0$ domain the producer surplus is
$PS_{0}=P^{*}(Q^{*}-q_{0})-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}dq$ and

$$
W_{0}=CS^{*}+PS_{0}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}q_{0}
      -\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq\approx
      32.7-6.66-9.9\approx15\!-\!17,
$$

about $W_{0}\simeq16$, $PS_{0}\simeq5.1$, $CS^{*}\simeq11.0$, which is the
net surplus measured from the zero-price choke quantity $q_{0}$.  The
$P^{*}q_{0}\approx6.66$ term is the difference between the gross
$W^{m}\approx22\!-\!23$ and the $P_{S}\ge0$ net $W_{0}\approx16$ figures
quoted in the literature. ∎

1.text:
The competitive clearing price is the unique root of

$$f(Q)=\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0 ,\qquad Q>\root3\of 2 ,$$

on the monotone increasing supply $P_{S}(Q)=\ln (Q^{3}-2)$ and the
monotone decreasing demand $P_{D}(Q)=18e^{-\arctan Q}$.
$f(4.5)<0<f(4.7)$ and a Newton iteration gives

$$Q^{*}\simeq4.68\!-\!4.70\approx4.69 ,\qquad 
P^{*}= \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq4.6\!-\!4.7,
$$

e.g. $Q^{*}\approx4.686$, $P^{*}\approx4.61\!-\!4.62$, $P^{*}Q^{*}
\approx21.6\!-\!21.7$.

With the inverse demand $Q_{D}(P)=\tan \!\left[\ln (18/P)\right]$

$$I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq
      =18\int_{0}^{T^{*} }e^{-T}\sec^{2}T dT ,
      \qquad T^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}\approx1.36 ,$$

$$I_{D}(Q^{*})\approx 3.24\!-\!3.28\times10^{1}\approx 32.5\!-\!32.8 .$$

On the mathematical branch of the supply $P_{S}(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$,
$q_{a}=\root3\of2\approx1.26$,

$$\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
   =\Big[q\ln(q^{3}-2)-3q-6\!\int\!\frac{dq}{q^{3}-2}\Big]_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}
   \approx 9.6\!-\!9.9 .$$

Hence on the textbook $CS+PS$ accounting with the improper supply
integral taken from the first real point $q_{a}$

$$CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.6\approx10.8\!-\!11.2,$$
$$PS_{g}^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
          \approx21.6-9.6\approx12.0\!-\!12.2,$$

and the gross area between demand and supply up to $Q^{*}$

$$W_{g}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{g}^{*}
        =I_{D}(Q^{*})-\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
        =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[P_{D}(q)-P_{S}(q)\big]_{+}dq
        \approx 22\!-\!24
$$

in $P\times Q$ units, e.g. $W_{g}^{*}\approx22.8\!-\!22.9$ with
$Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$, $CS^{*}\approx10.9$ and
$PS_{g}^{*}\approx12.0$.  This is the $ \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}
-\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}$ surplus normally quoted as the market
total surplus.

With the economically admissible non-negative supply convention
$P_{S}=0$ for $P_{S}<0$, i.e. $P_{S}(q_{0})=0$ with $q_{0}=\root3\of3
\approx1.442$,

$$PS_{0}^{*}=P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-q_{0}\right)-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
          \approx5.0\!-\!6.0,$$

$$W_{0}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{0}^{*}
         =I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}q_{0}-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
         \approx15\!-\!17,$$

about $W_{0}^{*}\approx16\!-\!17$ with $CS^{*}\approx11.0$ and
$PS_{0}^{*}\approx5.3$, the familiar $P^{*}q_{0}\approx6.6$ shift of the
gross $22\!-\!23$ figure.  The $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$
clearing is the same in either convention. ∎

10.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with the equilibrium part that is now essentially settled. 
ln(Q³-2)=18 e^{-arctan Q} is monotone on Q>∛2 and
Q*≈4.686-4.70, P*≈4.61-4.62 is reproduced by everyone, 
P*Q*≈21.6-21.7 and ∫₀^{Q*}18e^{-arctan q}dq≈32.5-32.8 on the usual Simpson/arctan quadrature.

Where the definition matters is the lower limit of the producer integral. 
P_S(q)=ln(q³-2) is real for q>∛2≈1.26 but it is negative on 
∛2<q<∛3≈1.442, P_S=0 at Q0=∛3. Economically a producer will not supply
at a negative price and the conventional textbook producer surplus is
measured from the zero-price choke Q0 where P_S first becomes non-negative.

With that economic choke

CS = ∫₀^{Q*} P_D(q)dq - P*Q*,
PS = ∫_{Q0}^{Q*} [P* - P_S(q)]dq
    = P*(Q* - Q0) - ∫_{Q0}^{Q*} ln(q³-2)dq,

so that the surplus actually realised on the traded interval is

TW_net = CS+PS
       = ∫₀^{Q*} P_D(q)dq - P*Q0 - ∫_{Q0}^{Q*} P_S(q)dq.

Using the numbers already quoted: 
∫₀^{Q*}18e^{-arctan q}dq≈32.47-32.70,
P*≈4.62, Q0=3^{1/3}≈1.442, P*Q0≈6.65-6.70,
∫_{Q0}^{Q*}ln(q³-2)dq≈9.8-10.0 on the same quadrature.
Hence

CS≈32.6-21.65≈10.9-11.0,
PS≈P*(Q*-Q0)-∫_{Q0}^{Q*}P_S≈14.99-9.9≈5.0-5.3,

TW_net≈∫₀^{Q*}P_D -P*Q0 -∫_{Q0}^{Q*}P_S≈32.6-6.7-9.9≈15.5-16.5.

That is the ≈16 units net surplus that C5 and C8 were pointing to when the
producer surplus is required to be non-negative, i.e. the familiar
∫_{Q0}^{Q*}[P*-P_S]dq measure. The ≈22-23–23.3 figures quoted by C1, C3,
C4, C6, C7, C10 are the gross area ∫₀^{Q*}P_D-∫_{q_a}^{Q*}P_S with
q_a=∛2 or Q0 absorbed in the P*Q* term; they contain the P*Q0≈6.6

5.text:
The clearing price is the unique intersection on the real branch
$Q^{3}>2$

$$P_{S}(Q)=P_{D}(Q)\iff 
\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q}\equiv P^{*},
\qquad Q>\sqrt[3]{2},$$

$f(Q)=\ln (Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}$ is monotone on the admissible
branch, $f(4.5)<0<f(4.7)$ and

$$Q^{*}\simeq 4.68\!-\!4.70\approx 4.69,
\qquad 
P^{*}= \ln\!\big(Q^{*3}-2\big)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx 4.61\!-\!4.62,
$$

e.g. $Q^{*}\approx4.686$, $P^{*}\approx4.614$.  Put
$W(q)=18e^{-\arctan q}$ and $C(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$, $q_{a}=\sqrt[3]{2}$.

$$

$$

     =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}W(q)dq-\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}C(q)dq
     =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}\!\Big[\,P_{D}(q)-P_{S}(q)\Big]_{+}dq .
$$

With $T=\arctan q$

$$

           =18\int_{0}^{T^{*}}e^{-T}\sec^{2}T\,dT\approx 32.4\!-\!32.8 ,
$$

$$
I_{S}^{a}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
               \approx 9.6\!-\!9.9 ,
$$

Hence

$$

$$

$$

and on the conventional gross $CS+PS$ accounting

$$
W^{*}_{g}=I_{D}-I_{S}^{a}\approx32.4\!-\!32.8-9.6\!-\!9.9
        \approx 22\!-\!24,

centrally

$$
W^{*}_{g}\approx 22.8\!-\!23.0,\qquad CS^{*}\approx 11.0,\;
PS^{a*}\approx 12.0,

With the textbook zero price choke $P_{S}(Q_{0})=0$,

i.e.

$$

$$
W_{g}^{*}\simeq 22.8\!-\!22.9,\qquad 
CS^{*}\simeq10.9,\qquad PS_{a}^{*}\simeq12.0,

at $Q^{*}\simeq4.69$, $P^{*}\simeq4.61$.  This is the $\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}

The market clearing price is the interior solution of

$$
P_{S}(Q)=P_{D}(Q)\iff 
\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q}\equiv P^{*},
\qquad Q>2^{1/3},
$$

so that with $f(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}$,
$f(4.5)<0<f(4.7)$ and a Newton iteration gives the unique admissible
root

$$Q^{*}\approx4.68\!-\!4.70\approx4.69 ,$$

$$P^{*}= \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx4.6\!-\!4.7,
\qquad P^{*}\simeq4.61\!-\!4.62,
$$

in the price units of the model.  In inverse form

$$
Q_{D}(P)=\tan\!\Big[\ln\frac{18}{P}\Big],\qquad 
Q_{S}(P)=\big(e^{P}+2\big)^{1/3}, 
$$

is the usual textbook notation.

On the traded interval the gross willingness to pay and the gross marginal
cost are

$$
W(q)=18e^{-\arctan q},\qquad C(q)=\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right),
\qquad q>q_{m}=2^{1/3}\simeq1.26,
$$

and with the conventional $CS+PS$ accounting

$$
CS(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}W(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*},\qquad
PS(Q^{*})=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}C(q)dq,
$$

so that on the traded interval

$$
W^{*}=CS+PS=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq .
$$

Now

$$
I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq
          =18\int_{0}^{\arctan Q^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt
          \approx 32.4\!-\!32.8,
$$

$$
P^{*}Q^{*}\approx4.62\times4.69\approx21.6\!-\!21.7,
$$

hence

$$
CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 10.8\!-\!11.0 .
$$

With the mathematical branch $q_{a}=q_{m}=2^{1/3}$

$$
I_{S}^{m}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{m}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
                \approx 9.6\!-\!9.9,
$$

so that

$$
PS^{m}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{S}^{m}\approx21.7-9.7\approx12.0\!-\!12.2
$$

and

$$
W^{m}=I_{D}-I_{S}^{m}\approx32.5-9.7\approx22\!-\!24,
$$

e.g. $W^{m}\simeq22.8$, $CS^{*}\simeq10.9$, $PS^{m}\simeq11.9$ for
$Q^{*}\simeq4.69$, $P^{*}\simeq4.62$.  This is the usual
$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}[P_{D}-P_{S}]dq$ area between the demand curve
$18e^{-\arctan q}$ and the inverse supply $\ln(q^{3}-2)$ up to the
competitive quantity, i.e. about $2.3\times10^{1}$ price$\times$
quantity units of gross social surplus.

Remark on the zero-price convention.  $P_{S}(q)=0$ at
$q_{0}=3^{1/3}\simeq1.44$.  On the economically admissible
$P_{S}\ge0$ domain the producer surplus is
$PS_{0}=P^{*}(Q^{*}-q_{0})-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}dq$ and

$$
W_{0}=CS^{*}+PS_{0}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}q_{0}
      -\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq\approx
      32.7-6.66-9.9\approx15\!-\!17,
$$

about $W_{0}\simeq16$, $PS_{0}\simeq5.1$, $CS^{*}\simeq11.0$, which is the
net surplus measured from the zero-price choke quantity $q_{0}$.  The
$P^{*}q_{0}\approx6.66$ term is the difference between the gross
$W^{m}\approx22\!-\!23$ and the $P_{S}\ge0$ net $W_{0}\approx16$ figures
quoted in the literature. ∎

TW_net≈∫₀^{Q*}P_D -P*Q0 -∫_{Q0}^{Q*}P_S≈32.6-6.7-9.9≈15.5-16.5.

public_text.6:
With the usual inverse notation $Q_{S}(P)=(e^{P}+2)^{1/3}$,
$Q_{D}(P)=\tan \!\left[\ln 18/P\right]$ the competitive price is

$$
P_{S}(Q)=P_{D}(Q)\iff 
\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q}\equiv P(Q),\qquad 
Q>\root3\of2 ,
$$

$$
f(Q)=\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0 .
$$

$f(4.5)<0<f(4.7)$ and a Newton iteration gives the unique economically
admissible root

$$
Q^{*}\simeq4.68\!-\!4.70,\qquad 
Q^{*}\approx4.69 ,
$$

$$
P^{*}= \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}
     \approx4.6\!-\!4.7,\qquad P^{*}\approx4.61\!-\!4.62,
$$
e.g. $Q^{*}\approx4.689$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$.
Put $W_{D}(q)=18e^{-\arctan q}$ and $C(q)=\ln \!\left(q^{3}-2\right)$ on the
real branch $q>q_{a}$, $q_{a}=\root3\of2\simeq1.26$.  On the traded
interval

$$
CS(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}W_{D}(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*},\qquad
PS(Q^{*})=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}C(q)dq ,
$$

so that the area between demand and (marginal-cost) supply up to $Q^{*}$
is

$$
W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}
     =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}W_{D}(q)dq-
      \int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}C(q)dq
     =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}\!\Big[18e^{-\arctan q}
       -\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)\Big]dq ,
$$
the improper supply integral being integrable at $q_{a}$.

With $t^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}\approx1.361$,

$$
I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq
          =18\int_{0}^{t^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt
          \approx 3.24\!-\!3.25\times10^{1},
$$

$$
I_{D}(Q^{*})\approx 32.4\!-\!32.8\approx32.5,
$$

and

$$
P^{*}Q^{*}\approx4.62\times4.69\approx21.6\!-\!21.7 .
$$

Hence

$$
CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.8\!-\!11.0
$$

in price$\times$quantity units.  On the real branch

$$
\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
   =\int_{q_{a}}^{q_{0}}\!\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
    +\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
    \approx-0.24+9.87\approx9.6\!-\!9.9,
$$

$q_{0}=\root3\of3\simeq1.442$ being the zero-price choke $P_{S}(q_{0})=0$.
Consequently

$$
PS_{g}^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}C(q)dq
        \approx21.7-9.6\!-\!9.9\approx11.8\!-\!12.2,
$$

and the gross $CS+PS$ surplus on the $0\to Q^{*}$ accounting is

$$
W_{g}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}
       =I_{D}(Q^{*})-\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}C(q)dq
       \approx 32.5-9.6\!-\!9.9\approx 22\!-\!24,
$$

e.g. with the $Q^{*}\approx4.69,\;P^{*}\approx4.62$ root

$$
I_{D}\approx32.45,\qquad 
\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}C\approx9.64,\qquad
W_{g}^{*}\approx22.8,
$$

$CS^{*}\approx10.9$, $PS_{g}^{*}\approx11.9$, $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.7$.
That is the $\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}[P_{D}-P_{S}]dq$ competitive surplus
normally quoted as $\simeq\$23$ at the $Q^{*}\approx4.7$, $P^{*}\approx4.6$
clearing point.

Remark.  On the textbook $P_{S}\ge0$ convention the producer surplus is
measured from the zero price choke $q_{0}=\root3\of3$.  Then

$$
PS_{0}^{*}=P^{*}(Q^{*}-q_{0})-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}C(q)dq
        \approx5.1\!-\!5.3,
$$

$$
TW_{0}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{0}^{*}
        =I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}q_{0}-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}C(q)dq
        \approx32.5-6.66-9.87\approx15.9\!-\!16.4,
$$

i.e. $\approx \$16$ of net $CS+PS$ measured from the $P_{S}=0$ point,
$CS^{*}\approx10.8\!-\!11.0$, $PS_{0}^{*}\approx5.1$, the $P^{*}q_{0}\approx
6.66$ shift being the difference between the gross $W_{g}^{*}\approx
22\!-\!23$ and the net $TW_{0}^{*}\approx15\!-\!16$ conventions.  The
$Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$ equilibrium is the same in both
conventions. ∎

1.text:
The clearing is settled.  On the real branch $Q>2^{1/3}$

$$P_{S}(Q)=\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right),\qquad P_{D}(Q)=18e^{-\arctan Q},$$

$$P_{S}(Q^{*})=P_{D}(Q^{*})\iff 
f(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0,$$

is monotone increasing for $Q>2^{1/3}$ and

$$f(4.5)<0<f(4.7),$$

so that with Newton / Simpson

$$Q^{*}\simeq 4.68\!-\!4.70\approx 4.69,\qquad
P^{*}= \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq4.61\!-\!4.62 ,$$

$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.6\!-\!21.7$.  Put $T=\arctan q$,

$$I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq
 =18\int_{0}^{T^{*}}e^{-T}\sec^{2}T\,dT\approx32.4\!-\!32.8\approx32.6, 
\qquad T^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}\approx1.36.$$

Hence on the textbook $CS+PS$ accounting

$$CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.6-21.7\approx10.8\!-\!11.2\approx\$11,$$

and with the mathematical branch point $q_{a}=2^{1/3}$

$$I_{S}^{a}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
 =\Big[q\ln(q^{3}-2)-3q-6\!\int\!\frac{dq}{q^{3}-2}\Big]_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}
 \approx9.6\!-\!9.9\approx9.7.$$

$$PS_{g}^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{S}^{a}(Q^{*})\approx21.7-9.7\approx12.0\!-\!12.2,$$

so that the area between demand and supply up to the clearing quantity

$$W_{g}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{g}^{*}
      =I_{D}(Q^{*})-I_{S}^{a}(Q^{*})
      =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[P_{D}(q)-P_{S}(q)\big]dq
      \approx32.6-9.7\approx22\!-\!24,$$

e.g. $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$,

$I_{D}\approx32.5$, $I_{S}^{a}\approx9.7$, $CS^{*}\approx10.9$, $PS_{g}^{*}\approx12.0$,

$$W_{g}^{*}\approx22.8\!-\!22.9\approx23.0$$

in $P\times Q$ units.  This is the conventional $\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}
-\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}$ gross total surplus quoted in the literature; 
$Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$, $CS^{*}\approx11$ is stable.

Remark on the economically admissible convention.  $P_{S}(q)=0$ at
$q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442$, so that on the $P_{S}\ge0$ choke

$$PS_{0}^{*}=P^{*}(Q^{*}-q_{0})-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq\approx5.0\!-\!5.3,$$

$$W_{0}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{0}^{*}
      =I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}q_{0}-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
      \approx32.6-6.66-9.9\approx15\!-\!17\approx16.4,$$

the familiar $P^{*}q_{0}\approx6.6$ shift between the gross $W_{g}^{*}\approx
22\!-\!23$ and the net $P_{S}\ge0$ $W_{0}^{*}\approx16$ accounting.  The
clearing $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$ is common to both conventions.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The equilibrium root is now stable for everyone. 
$f(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0$, $Q>2^{1/3}$, is monotone and
$f(4.5)<0<f(4.7)$ gives

$Q^{*}\simeq4.68\!-\!4.70$, $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, 
$P^{*}= \ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx4.61\!-\!4.64$, 
$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.6\!-\!21.7$,

and

$I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq
      =18\int_{0}^{\arctan Q^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t dt\approx32.4\!-\!32.8$,

so $CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx10.8\!-\!11.1$ is robust.

Where the welfare accounting diverges is the lower limit of the producer
integral. $P_{S}(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$ is real for $q>q_{a}=2^{1/3}\approx1.260$
but $P_{S}(q)<0$ on $q_{a}<q<Q_{0}$ with

$P_{S}(Q_{0})=0\iff Q_{0}^{3}=3,\qquad Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442$,

the zero-price choke. On $q_{a}<q<Q_{0}$ marginal cost is negative, the
supply curve is below the horizontal axis and a producer will not supply
at a negative price. Textbook producer surplus is defined on the
economically admissible set $P_{S}\ge0$, i.e. on $[Q_{0},Q^{*}]$, not on the
mathematical branch $[q_{a},Q^{*}]$.

With the non-negative convention

$PS_{0}=P^{*}(Q^{*}-Q_{0})-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq$,

$TW_{net}=CS^{*}+PS_{0}
        =I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q_{0}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq$.

Numerically with the common root $Q^{*}\approx4.686\!-\!4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$,

$P^{*}Q_{0}\approx4.62\times1.442\approx6.65\!-\!6.70$,

$\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.8\!-\!10.0$,

hence

$CS^{*}\approx32.6-21.65\approx10.9\!-\!11.0$,

$PS_{0}=P^{*}(Q^{*}-Q_{0})-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}\approx14.99-9.9\approx5.0\!-\!5.3$,

$TW_{net}\approx32.6-6.7-9.9\approx15.5\!-\!16.5$,

about $16.0\!-\!16.4$ with the Simpson quadratures used by C5, C7, C8 and C10.
This is the $Q^{*}-Q_{0}$ producer surplus and the familiar $P^{*}Q_{0}\approx6.6$
shift down from the formal area $\,I_{D}(Q^{*})-\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}\approx22\!-\!23$.

The $\approx22.8$ gross figure $W_{g}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}$ is
the mathematical area between $P_{D}$ and $P_{S}$ up to $Q^{*}$; it contains
the negative marginal-cost tail $\int_{q_{a}}^{Q_{0}}P_{S}(q)dq<0$ and a
rectangular $P^{*}Q_{0}$ shift that corresponds to non-producible quantity.
Once $P_{S}<0$ is set to zero as it must be for a real production set, the
economically meaningful total surplus at the competitive clearing
$Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$ is the net $\approx1.6\times10^{1}$
units, $CS\approx11$, $PS_{0}\approx5$, $TW_{net}\approx16$, i.e. the
$\approx15\!-\!17$ net welfare quoted above. ∎

\qquad T^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}\approx1.36,
$$

$$
I_{D}(Q^{*})\approx32.4\!-\!32.8\approx32.5\!-\!32.7 .
$$

Hence the textbook gross consumer surplus

$$
CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.6-21.65\approx10.8\!-\!11.2,
$$

about $CS^{*}\approx10.9\!-\!11.0$ on the $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$
root.

On the mathematical branch $q_{a}=2^{1/3}$

$$
I_{S}^{a}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
       =\Big[q\ln(q^{3}-2)-3q-6\!\int\!\frac{dq}{q^{3}-2}\Big]_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}
       \approx9.6\!-\!9.9\approx9.7 .
$$

The conventional gross $CS+PS$ area between the two inverse curves up to
$Q^{*}$ is

$$
W_{g}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{g}^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-I_{S}^{a}(Q^{*})
        =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[P_{D}(q)-P_{S}(q)\big]_{+}dq ,
$$

$$
PS_{g}^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{S}^{a}(Q^{*})\approx21.65-9.7\approx12.0\!-\!12.2,
$$

$$
W_{g}^{*}\approx32.6-9.7\approx22\!-\!24,
$$

about $W_{g}^{*}\simeq22.8\!-\!22.9$ with

$Q^{*}\simeq4.69,\;P^{*}\simeq4.62,\;CS^{*}\simeq10.9,\;PS_{g}^{*}\simeq12.0$,
the usual $\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}-\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}$ total surplus
quoted by C1-C6, C8-C9.

Remark on the economic $P_{S}\ge0$ convention. $P_{S}(q_{0})=0$ at
$q_{0}=3^{1/3}\simeq1.442$.  Measured from the zero-price choke

$$
PS_{0}^{*}=P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-q_{0}\right)-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
        \approx5.0\!-\!5.5,
$$

$$
W_{0}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{0}^{*}
       =I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}q_{0}-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
       \approx15\!-\!17,
$$

e.g. $W_{0}^{*}\approx16.0\!-\!16.5$, $CS^{*}\approx11.0$, $PS_{0}^{*}
\approx5.1\!-\!5.3$, the $P^{*}q_{0}\approx6.66$ shift of the gross
$22\!-\!23$ figure.  The $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$ clearing
is unchanged; the $\approx22.8$ figure is the area-between-curves total
welfare normally reported, the $\approx16$ figure being the net
$P_{S}\ge0$ producer surplus measured from $q_{0}=3^{1/3}$. ∎

3.text:
The clearing price is the unique admissible root of

on $P_{S}(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)$ strictly increasing and

      \simeq4.61\!-\!4.62, $$

$$I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq
      =18\int_{0}^{T^{*}}e^{-T}\sec^{2}T\,dT,
      \qquad T^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}\simeq1.361, $$

$$I_{D}(Q^{*})\approx32.4\!-\!32.8\approx32.6, $$

so that with the usual inverse-surplus notation

$$CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}
       \approx32.6-21.7\approx10.8\!-\!11.2\approx \$10.9 .$$

   =\Big[q\ln(q^{3}-2)-3q-6\!\int\!\frac{dq}{q^{3}-2}\Big]_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}
   \approx9.6\!-\!9.9\approx9.7 .$$

$$PS_{g}^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{S}^{a}(Q^{*})\approx21.7-9.7\approx12.0\!-\!12.2,

and the area between the two inverse curves up to $Q^{*}$

e.g. $Q^{*}\approx4.69,\;P^{*}\approx4.62,\;
CS^{*}\approx10.9,\;PS_{g}^{*}\approx12.0,\;
W_{g}^{*}\approx22.8\!-\!22.9$ in $P\times Q$ units, the
$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}-\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}$ total surplus normally

$q_{0}=3^{1/3}\simeq1.442$.  On the $P_{S}\ge0$ economic convention

figure is the $P^{*}q_{0}\approx6.6$ shift above the net

          =18\int_{0}^{T^{*}}e^{-T}\sec^{2}T\,dT,

      \approx 32.6-21.7\approx 10.8\!-\!11.2\approx \$11 ,

\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq\approx9.8\!-\!10.0,

$$
\int_{Q_{a}}^{Q_{0}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
      =\Big[(q-Q_{a})\ln\!\big(3Q_{a}^{2}(q-Q_{a})\big)-(q-Q_{a})\Big]_{0}^{Q_{0}-Q_{a}}

$$
I_{S}^{a}(Q^{*})\approx 9.6\!-\!9.9\approx9.7,
$$

and the gross area between the two inverse curves up to $Q^{*}$ is

$$
W_{g}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{g}^{*}
        =I_{D}(Q^{*})-I_{S}^{a}(Q^{*})
        =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}\!\!\big[P_{D}(q)-P_{S}(q)\big]dq,
$$

$$
PS_{g}^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{S}^{a}(Q^{*})\approx21.7-9.7\approx12.0\!-\!12.2,
$$
$$
W_{g}^{*}\approx32.5-9.7\approx22.5\!-\!23.5,
$$

f(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0,$$

is monotone increasing for $Q>2^{1/3}$ and

$$f(4.5)<0<f(4.7),$$

so that with Newton / Simpson

$$I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq
 =18\int_{0}^{T^{*}}e^{-T}\sec^{2}T\,dT\approx32.4\!-\!32.8\approx32.6,

 \approx9.6\!-\!9.9\approx9.7.$$

so that the area between demand and supply up to the clearing quantity

$$W_{g}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{g}^{*}
      =I_{D}(Q^{*})-I_{S}^{a}(Q^{*})
      =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[P_{D}(q)-P_{S}(q)\big]dq
      \approx32.6-9.7\approx22\!-\!24,$$

$$W_{g}^{*}\approx22.8\!-\!22.9\approx23.0$$

in $P\times Q$ units.  This is the conventional $\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}

The clearing price is the unique solution of the monotone
intersection

$$
P_{S}(Q)=P_{D}(Q)\iff 
\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q}\equiv P^{*},
\qquad Q^{3}>2 ,
$$

$ f(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}$ is strictly increasing on the
real branch $Q>2^{1/3}$ and $f(4.5)<0<f(4.7)$.  Newton/Simpson

$$
Q^{*}\simeq 4.68\!-\!4.70\approx 4.69,\qquad 
P^{*}= \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}
      \simeq 4.61\!-\!4.64\approx 4.62 ,
$$

$$
P^{*}Q^{*}\simeq 4.62\times 4.69\simeq 21.6\!-\!21.7 .
$$

Put $W(q)=18e^{-\arctan q}$ and $C(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$.
With $T=\arctan q$,

$$
I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}W(q)dq
          =18\int_{0}^{T^{*}}e^{-T}\sec^{2}T\,dT,
\qquad T^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}\approx1.36,
$$

$$
I_{D}(Q^{*})\approx 32.4\!-\!32.8\approx32.5\!-\!32.7 .
$$

Hence the textbook consumer surplus on $0\to Q^{*}$

$$
CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}
      \approx 32.6-21.7\approx 10.8\!-\!11.2\approx \$11 ,
$$

which is robust to the supply convention.

On the real log branch $q_{a}=2^{1/3}\simeq1.260$

$$
I_{S}^{a}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
        \approx 9.6\!-\!9.9\approx 9.7 ,
$$

so that with the usual mathematical $CS+PS$ accounting

$$
PS_{g}^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{S}^{a}(Q^{*})\approx21.7-9.7\approx
12.0\!-\!12.2,
$$

and the gross area between the inverses up to $Q^{*}$

$$
W_{g}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{g}^{*}
       =I_{D}(Q^{*})-\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
       \approx 32.6-9.7\approx 22\!-\!24,
$$

e.g. $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$, 
$I_{D}\approx32.5$, $\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}\approx9.7$,

$$
W_{g}^{*}\simeq 22.8\!-\!22.9,\qquad CS^{*}\simeq10.9,\qquad 
PS_{g}^{*}\simeq12.0,
$$

the $\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}-\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}$ total surplus
normally quoted as $\sim2.3\times10^{1}$ $P\times Q$ units.

Remark on the economic choke.  $P_{S}(q)=0$ at $q_{0}=3^{1/3}\simeq1.442$.
With the $P_{S}\ge0$ convention

$$
PS_{0}^{*}=P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-q_{0}\right)-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
        \approx5.0\!-\!5.5,
$$

$$
W_{0}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{0}^{*}
       =I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}q_{0}-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
       \approx32.6-6.66-9.9\approx15.5\!-\!16.8,
$$

about $W_{0}^{*}\approx16.0\!-\!16.5$, $CS^{*}\approx11.0$, $PS_{0}^{*}
\approx5.1\!-\!5.3$, i.e. the familiar $P^{*}q_{0}\approx6.6$ shift of
the gross $22\!-\!23$ figure.  The clearing $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, 
$P^{*}\approx4.62$ is unchanged; the $\approx22.8$ gross area is the
textbook $\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}[P_{D}-P_{S}]dq$ total welfare, which becomes
the economically non-negative $\approx16$ net surplus once the negative

public_text.2:
With the inverse form $P_{S}(Q)=\ln (Q^{3}-2),\;Q>Q_{a}$,
$Q_{a}=2^{1/3}$ and $P_{D}(Q)=18e^{-\arctan Q}$ the competitive
intersection is

$$
\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q}\equiv P^{*},\qquad 
Q^{*}>Q_{a},
$$

$f(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}$ is strictly increasing on the
real branch, $f(4.5)<0<f(4.7)$ and Newton gives

$$
Q^{*}\simeq4.69\!-\!4.70,\qquad Q^{*}\approx4.695,
$$
$$
P^{*}= \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx4.62,
\qquad P^{*}Q^{*}\approx4.621\times4.695\approx 21.7
$$
in the $P\times Q$ units of the model.  Put $t=\arctan q$. Then

$$
I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq
          =18\int_{0}^{T^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt,\qquad 
T^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}\approx1.361,
$$

and on the $0\to Q^{*}$ Simpson quadrature

$$
I_{D}(Q^{*})\approx 32.4\!-\!33.0\approx 32.5,
$$

so that on the usual textbook $CS$ definition

$$
CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 32.5-21.7\approx10.8\!-\!11.0,
$$
e.g. $CS^{*}\simeq10.9$ with $Q^{*}\simeq4.69$, $P^{*}\simeq4.62$.

On the real branch

$$
I_{S}^{a}(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
   =\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
    +\int_{Q_{a}}^{Q_{0}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq ,
$$
$Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\simeq1.442$ being the zero price choke
$P_{S}(Q_{0})=0$.  With the Simpson rule on the non–negative part

$$
\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq\approx9.8\!-\!10.0,
$$

and

$$
\int_{Q_{a}}^{Q_{0}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
      =\Big[(q-Q_{a})\ln\!\big(3Q_{a}^{2}(q-Q_{a})\big)-(q-Q_{a})\Big]_{0}^{Q_{0}-Q_{a}}
      \approx-0.19\!-\!0.24 .
$$

Hence in the mathematical $q_{a}=2^{1/3}$ convention

$$
I_{S}^{a}(Q^{*})\approx 9.6\!-\!9.9\approx9.7,
$$

and the gross area between the two inverse curves up to $Q^{*}$ is

$$
W_{g}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{g}^{*}
        =I_{D}(Q^{*})-I_{S}^{a}(Q^{*})
        =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}\!\!\big[P_{D}(q)-P_{S}(q)\big]dq,
$$

$$
PS_{g}^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{S}^{a}(Q^{*})\approx21.7-9.7\approx12.0\!-\!12.2,
$$
$$
W_{g}^{*}\approx32.5-9.7\approx22.5\!-\!23.5,
$$

e.g. with the $Q^{*}\approx4.695,\;P^{*}\approx4.621$ root

$$
I_{D}\approx32.5,\qquad I_{S}^{a}\approx9.70,\qquad
CS^{*}\approx10.8,\qquad PS_{g}^{*}\approx12.0,\qquad
W_{g}^{*}\approx22.8,
$$

the $\approx 2.3\times10^{1}$ $P\times Q$ units normally quoted as the
market total surplus, $CS^{*}\approx\$11$ and $PS_{g}^{*}\approx\$12$
at the competitive clearing $Q^{*}\approx4.7$, $P^{*}\approx4.6$.

Imposing the economically admissible $P_{S}\ge0$ convention,
$P_{S}\equiv0$ for $Q<Q_{0}$, the producer surplus is measured from the
zero price choke

$$
PS_{0}^{*}=P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-Q_{0}\right)-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq,
$$
$$
W_{0}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{0}^{*}
        =I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q_{0}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq,
$$

i.e.

$$
PS_{0}^{*}\approx P^{*}(Q^{*}-Q_{0})-9.90\approx5.0\!-\!5.5,
$$
$$
W_{0}^{*}\approx32.5-6.67-9.90\approx15.9\!-\!16.5,
$$

about $W_{0}^{*}\simeq16$ with $CS^{*}\simeq11.0$ and
$PS_{0}^{*}\simeq5.1$.  The $P^{*}Q_{0}\approx6.66$ rectangular shift is
the difference $W_{g}^{*}-W_{0}^{*}$ between the usual
$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}-\int_{Q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}$ gross area and the
$P_{S}\ge0$ net surplus.  The clearing $Q^{*}\approx4.69$,
$P^{*}\approx4.62$ is the same in either accounting; the $\approx22\!-\!23$
figure is the conventional area-between-curves total welfare, $\approx
16$ the net $CS+PS$ measured from the $P_{S}=0$ choke $Q_{0}=3^{1/3}$. ∎

$CS^{*}=I_D(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.6-21.65\approx10.9-11.1\approx\$11$.
